_comment: The Android path configuration. It expresses the same routing decisions as
ios_path_configuration.json — which screens are modal, which get
pull-to-refresh — but it is NOT a copy of it, and the two differences below
are why it cannot be one.
DIFFERENCE 1: every rule needs a `uri`. Android builds a navigation graph of
Fragments, so a rule has to name the fragment destination to instantiate.
The catch-all supplies `hotwire://fragment/web` (plus `fallback_uri` for a
destination that fails to resolve); lesson screens override it with
`hotwire://fragment/web/lesson`, which is the fragment that draws the native
close X. iOS picks its view controller in Swift instead
(SceneDelegate.isLessonURL), so its file has no `uri` anywhere.
DIFFERENCE 2: patterns are matched against the path AND query string, and
unlike iOS there is no switch to turn that off. iOS sets
Hotwire.config.pathConfiguration.matchQueryStrings = false in SceneDelegate,
so a `$`-anchored pattern there means what it looks like it means. Android's
PathConfigurationData always matches against `path?query` when a query is
present, so a bare `$` anchor fails for every link carrying one — and this
app appends ?lang= to almost everything. Each anchored pattern below
therefore ends with `(\?.*)?$` rather than `$`. Forgetting that suffix on a
new rule does not error; the screen just quietly presents as a plain push.
ORDER MATTERS, AND NOT THE WAY IT LOOKS, exactly as on iOS. Hotwire Native
merges the properties of every rule whose pattern matches, with LATER rules
winning (PathConfigurationData#properties: `properties.putAll(rule.properties)`),
and patterns are unanchored regexes, so `.*` matches every path. The
catch-all therefore has to come FIRST, as the baseline that specific rules
below override. Keep the most specific rules at the bottom.
The tab roots (/app, /app/library) deliberately carry no rule of their own:
MainActivity draws a native BottomNavigationView with one NavigatorHost per
tab, so those are plain default-context visits. The Create tab's root is
/app/import_requests/new instead of the bare /app/import_requests (which has
no route at all), so it relies on the 'Add a video' rule below rather than
being rule-free like the other two roots.
This file is served to the app by ConfigurationsController and must stay
identical to langlets-android/app/src/main/assets/json/path_configuration.json,
which is the offline fallback. A test enforces it.
Authentication is a default-context replace_root flow, not a modal. There
is no useful screen behind login for a signed-out user to dismiss back to.
The route handler and the rendered auth layout both hide bottom navigation;
the layout assertion also covers server redirects whose destination was not
visible in the original native proposal.
Add a video is deliberately context 'default', i.e. a plain push inside the
Create tab with the back arrow and bottom navigation intact. It needs its
own rule to escape the '/new' modal pattern above it — and that same rule is
what lets this path double as the Create tab's root.
review_lessons and review_lesson_builds are both modal, matching the course
lesson rule above: taking a review lesson is one continuous session from the
tap on 'Review words' through the waiting screen to the activities and the
finish page, and it should present and dismiss as a single modal context with
the tab bar hidden throughout rather than flash the tab bar during the wait.
review_lesson_builds needs its own pattern because the '_builds' suffix means
it doesn't match '/review_lessons/.*'.
The Pro paywall and its confirmation are one modal context, sharing a stack:
the purchase POST navigates from /app/pro to /app/pro/success, and both being
modal keeps that inside the screen the user opened rather than dropping them
back onto Home mid-purchase. Note that Pro cannot actually be BOUGHT on
Android — the apple-purchase bridge component has no counterpart here — so
this is presentation only until Play Billing is wired up.
